name: vb2_core_reqbufs
prose: Precondition: q and count point to valid objects owned by the caller; the function takes q->mmap_lock only around the free and storage steps and holds no lock on return. Postcondition: it returns -EBUSY with no state changed if q->streaming is set, or if q->waiting_in_dqbuf is set and *count is non-zero. If *count is 0, or q already has buffers, or q->memory is set and differs from memory, or non_coherent_mem (from V4L2_MEMORY_FLAG_NON_COHERENT in flags) differs from q->non_coherent_mem, it cancels the queue, frees every buffer slot up to q->max_num_buffers under q->mmap_lock and clears q->is_busy; if *count is 0 it then returns 0 without calling queue_setup (q->memory is reset to VB2_MEMORY_UNKNOWN by the free once no buffers remain). Otherwise it takes num_buffers as *count raised to at least q->min_reqbufs_allocation and capped at q->max_num_buffers, allocates q->bufs and q->bufs_bitmap if they are NULL, and sets q->memory to memory; if that storage allocation fails it returns -ENOMEM with q->memory already set to memory and no buffers allocated. It then sets q->non_coherent_mem to non_coherent_mem only when q->allow_cache_hints is set and q->memory is VB2_MEMORY_MMAP (else 0), and calls the driver queue_setup. If queue_setup returns non-zero, reports zero planes or a zero plane size, or the first buffer allocation returns zero buffers (-ENOMEM), it sets q->memory to VB2_MEMORY_UNKNOWN, frees q->bufs and q->bufs_bitmap and returns that error. If fewer than q->min_reqbufs_allocation buffers were allocated it frees those buffers and returns -ENOMEM; if fewer than requested but at least the minimum, it calls queue_setup a second time with the reduced count and plane count 0, and a non-zero return from it, or a count still larger than what was allocated (-ENOMEM), also frees the allocated buffers and returns the error; in these three cases the bufs and bufs_bitmap storage is not freed and q->memory is reset only by the free when no buffers remain in q. On success it sets *count to the number of buffers allocated, q->waiting_for_buffers to !q->is_output and q->is_busy to 1, and returns 0.
note: Reviewer 1 (early returns do not free) right for the original prose; reviewer 2 claims (second queue_setup -ENOMEM, non_coherent conditional on cache hints) right and now covered. Previous prose wrongly said storage freed/memory reset in all failure cases (lines 1005-1016 do not free storage). videobuf2-core.c:873-1035, callees 829-863, 584-698.

name: dvb_demux_do_ioctl
prose: Precondition: file->private_data points to a valid dmxdev_filter whose dev is a valid dmxdev, and parg points to the argument structure for cmd (struct dmx_filter, dmx_pes_filter_params, u16 pid, dmx_stc, dmx_pes_pids, or the vb2 structures for the buffer commands); the caller holds neither dmxdev->mutex nor the filter mutex. Postcondition: it first takes dmxdev->mutex interruptibly and returns -ERESTARTSYS without holding anything if interrupted. DMX_START, DMX_STOP, DMX_SET_FILTER, DMX_SET_PES_FILTER, DMX_SET_BUFFER_SIZE, DMX_ADD_PID, DMX_REMOVE_PID and, under CONFIG_DVB_MMAP, DMX_REQBUFS, DMX_QUERYBUF, DMX_EXPBUF, DMX_QBUF and DMX_DQBUF also take the filter's own mutex interruptibly; if that is interrupted the result is -ERESTARTSYS (dmxdev->mutex is released first or on the common exit) and nothing else is run, otherwise the filter mutex is released after the operation. DMX_GET_PES_PIDS, DMX_GET_STC and unknown commands run holding only dmxdev->mutex. Return values: for DMX_START, -EINVAL if the filter state is below DMXDEV_STATE_SET, else the result of dvb_dmxdev_filter_start; for DMX_STOP, DMX_SET_FILTER, DMX_SET_PES_FILTER, DMX_SET_BUFFER_SIZE, DMX_ADD_PID and DMX_REMOVE_PID the result of the matching dvb_dmxdev_* helper; for DMX_GET_PES_PIDS, -EINVAL if the demux has no get_pes_pids callback, else 0 (the callback is called and its result is not used); for DMX_GET_STC, -EINVAL if the demux has no get_stc callback, else the callback's return; for the vb2 commands the matching dvb_vb2_* result, except that for DMX_QBUF a zero result with the context not streaming is replaced by the result of dvb_vb2_stream_on; if CONFIG_DVB_MMAP is off those vb2 commands fall into the default case; an unknown command returns -ENOTTY. dmxdev->mutex is released before every return that follows its acquisition.
note: Reviewer claims across 3 rounds all right (GET_PES_PIDS/GET_STC hold only dmxdev->mutex 1092-1109; GET_PES_PIDS ignores return 1097; DMX_START return value 1049-1052 omitted). dmxdev.c:1032-1183.

name: dvb_frontend_start
prose: Precondition: fe is a valid frontend whose frontend_priv points to an initialized dvb_frontend_private, and fe->dvb and fe->id are valid. Postcondition: if fepriv->thread is non-NULL and fe->exit is DVB_FE_NO_EXIT it returns 0 and changes nothing. If fepriv->thread is non-NULL and fe->exit is anything else, it calls dvb_frontend_stop(fe) first; that sets fe->exit to DVB_FE_NORMAL_EXIT unless it is DVB_FE_DEVICE_REMOVED, and when fepriv->thread is non-NULL it calls kthread_stop, re-initialises fepriv->sem to a count of 1 and sets fepriv->state to FESTATE_IDLE. It then returns -EINTR if signal_pending(current) is true or if down_interruptible(&fepriv->sem) is interrupted; on those returns it does not take the semaphore, but any effects of the preceding dvb_frontend_stop call remain. Otherwise it holds fepriv->sem, sets fepriv->state to FESTATE_IDLE, fe->exit to DVB_FE_NO_EXIT and fepriv->thread to NULL, and starts the kernel thread dvb_frontend_thread with kthread_run. If kthread_run fails it releases fepriv->sem with up() and returns the negative error from PTR_ERR; on success it stores the thread in fepriv->thread and returns 0 with fepriv->sem still taken (nothing in this function releases it; dvb_frontend_stop re-initialises it later).
note: Reviewer 1 right on early return/-EINTR not changing state (original prose); reviewer 2 right (stop may run before -EINTR, 868-874); reviewer 3 right: sem is not released by start; only sema_init in dvb_frontend_stop:824 resets it (grep of fepriv->sem shows no up() other than 888). dvb_frontend.c:856-893.

name: cx22702_set_tps
prose: Precondition: fe is a valid dvb_frontend whose demodulator_priv points to an initialized cx22702_state and whose dtv_property_cache holds the requested parameters. Postcondition: if fe->ops.tuner_ops.set_params is set it is called (its result is ignored) and then fe->ops.i2c_gate_ctrl(fe, 0) is called if that hook is set; the inversion setting from p->inversion is applied through cx22702_set_inversion and its return value, including an error for INVERSION_AUTO, is ignored. If p->bandwidth_hz is not 6000000, 7000000 or 8000000 the function returns -EINVAL, after those earlier tuner and inversion actions. Otherwise it rewrites register 0x0C with its bits 4 and 5 replaced according to the bandwidth (0x20 for 6 MHz, 0x10 for 7 MHz, none for 8 MHz), and sets p->code_rate_LP to FEC_AUTO in the property cache. Because code_rate_LP is then FEC_AUTO, the auto branch is always taken: it writes 0x10, 0x09 and 0xC1 to registers 0x06, 0x07 and 0x08, clears the low two bits of register 0x0B, sets bit 6 of register 0x0C, writes 0x01 to register 0x00 to begin acquisition, and returns 0. The manual-programming code after that branch (with its -EINVAL returns for modulation, hierarchy, code rates, guard interval and transmission mode) is not reachable. Register write and read failures are not checked and no locks are taken or released.
note: Slice cut the head and the packet name was wrong: real function is cx22702_set_tps (cx22702.c:251-419), registered as .set_frontend at line 628. Mechanical reason 'name not in slice' was right about the name; existing prose described the correct body. Reviewer: mechanical, counted as right.

name: cx24110_diseqc_send_burst
prose: Precondition: fe is a valid dvb_frontend whose demodulator_priv points to a cx24110_state. Postcondition: if burst is neither SEC_MINI_A nor SEC_MINI_B it returns -EINVAL before any register access. For SEC_MINI_A (bit value 0x00) or SEC_MINI_B (bit value 0x08) it reads register 0x77 and, if bit 0x04 is clear, writes it back with that bit set; it then reads register 0x76 and writes back ((value & 0x90) | 0x40 | bit value), and busy-waits, re-reading register 0x76 repeatedly, until bit 0x40 of that register reads as set or 100 ms of jiffies have passed. It returns 0 after the wait whether the bit was seen or the timeout expired; register read and write results are not checked.
note: Reviewer 3 right: loop at cx24110.c:392 continues while bit 0x40 is NOT set, so it waits for the bit to become set (old prose said clear). Reviewers 1 and 2 were about the formal contract (now empty) - not verifiable claims about prose; counted as right in spirit. Loop is a busy-wait with no sleep. cx24110.c:371-396.

name: cx24120_init
prose: Precondition: fe is a frontend whose demodulator_priv points to an allocated cx24120_state with a usable I2C adapter, and state->config->request_firmware is a valid callback. Postcondition: if state->cold_init is already non-zero it returns 0 without touching the hardware. Otherwise it writes a fixed register initialisation sequence and then calls request_firmware for CX24120_FIRMWARE; if that returns non-zero it returns that code with state->cold_init still clear and no firmware to release. On success it uploads the firmware to the chip, sleeps 500 ms, reads register 0xe1 and compares it with the last firmware byte, writes 0x00 to register 0xdc and calls release_firmware (this release happens once on both the match and the mismatch path, before any later return); on a mismatch it returns -EREMOTEIO. It then sends CMD_START_TUNER (-EREMOTEIO if the send is non-zero), calls cx24120_set_vco (returns its non-zero result), sends CMD_BANDWIDTH (-EREMOTEIO on failure), reads register 0xba and returns -EREMOTEIO if the value is above 3, configures the MPEG outputs with the global config and the three output configs (-EREMOTEIO if any returns non-zero), sends CMD_BER_CTRL for the BER window (-EREMOTEIO on failure), and reads the four firmware version bytes with CMD_FWVERSION, returning the message-send result if one is non-zero. On reaching the end it sets the strength, cnr, post_bit_error, post_bit_count, block_error and block_count statistics in the property cache to length 1 with scale FE_SCALE_NOT_AVAILABLE, sets state->cold_init to 1 and returns 0. On every error return after the register sequence, cold_init stays 0 and the register writes already made are not undone. Register read and write results during the sequences and the firmware upload are not checked.
note: Slice cut the head and the packet name was wrong: real function is cx24120_init (cx24120.c:1269-1467). Existing prose was accurate (release_firmware at 1364 before the 1365 return) and kept with additions. Reviewer: mechanical name issue, counted right.

name: x_tune2
prose: Precondition: if tnr_dmd is non-NULL, tnr_dmd->io is a valid register-access table with write_reg, write_regs and read_regs callbacks (they are used without a NULL check). Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL if tnr_dmd is NULL, with no register access. Otherwise it performs, in order, and returns the first non-zero result of any step without doing the later ones: write SYS register 0x00 = 0x11; write SYS registers 0x2d..0x2f = 0x01, 0x0e, 0x01; write the x_tune2_seq1 table to SYS; read one byte from SYS register 0x2c; write SYS register 0x00 = 0x10; write the byte read from 0x2c to SYS register 0x60; write the x_tune2_seq2 table to SYS; write the x_tune2_seq3 table to DMD. If shift_frequency_khz is non-zero it then writes DMD register 0x00 = 0xe1, reads two bytes at DMD 0x60, adds shift_frequency_khz*1000 divided by 183 (clock modes A, C and any other value) or 178 (clock mode B), rounded to nearest, to the 16-bit two's-complement value read, clamps the sum to [-32768, 32767] and writes it back to DMD 0x60..0x61; it then reads DMD register 0x69, adds -shift_frequency_khz*1000 divided by 17578 or 17090 (bandwidth CXD2880_DTV_BW_1_7_MHZ, clock mode A/C/other versus B) or by 35156 or 34180 (other bandwidths, same clock-mode split), rounded to nearest, to the 8-bit two's-complement value read, clamps the sum to [-128, 127] and writes it to DMD register 0x69. If tnr_dmd->create_param.stationary_use is true it writes the x_tune2_seq4 table to DMD. It finally returns the result of writing the x_tune2_seq5 table to DMD, which is 0 on success or that write's error code.
note: Reviewer 4 right: old prose omitted unconditional SYS 0x2c read, SYS 0x00=0x10 write and the 0x60 write, and said 0x11 only (cxd2880_tnrdmd.c:1025-1063). The 'name outside slice' mechanical note was about the slice only; x_tune2 is a real static function at 1014-1219. Return value is the last seq5 write (1215).

name: rf_init1
prose: Precondition: if tnr_dmd is non-NULL, tnr_dmd->io is a valid register-access table; tnr_dmd->lna_thrs_tbl_air, if non-NULL, holds at least 24 thrs entries and tnr_dmd->lna_thrs_tbl_cable, if non-NULL, holds at least 32 (the loops index idx 0..23 and 0..31). Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL if tnr_dmd is NULL, before any register access. Otherwise it runs a long fixed series of SYS and DMD register writes (including constant tables, chip_id and stationary_use / is_cxd2881gg dependent values, and the LNA threshold tables, where a NULL table leaves the default bytes for that block in place), returning the first non-zero I/O result at once; earlier writes are not undone. It sleeps with usleep_range(1000, 2000) three times and checks bit 0 of three read-back registers: SYS bank 0x0a register 0x10 (after the first sleep), SYS bank 0x0a register 0x11 (after the second) and SYS bank 0x1a register 0x10 (after the third); if any of those bits is clear it returns -EINVAL at that point without doing the later writes. If all checks pass it returns the result of writing the rf_init1_seq9 table to SYS, which is 0 on success or that write's error code.
note: Reviewer 4 wrong on both points: NULL tnr_dmd is explicitly handled with -EINVAL (rf_init1 line 437-438) and there is a third bit check (lines 818-829); the old prose was right on those. The old prose was wrong in saying two sleeps and returning 0 only after all writes: there are three usleep_range calls (727, 749, 816) and the final return is the seq9 write result (831). cxd2880_tnrdmd.c:391-835 (read fully).

name: x_tune_dvbt2_demod_setting
prose: Precondition: if tnr_dmd is non-NULL, tnr_dmd->io is a valid register-access table; bandwidth and clk_mode should be enum values the function handles. Postcondition: this is the DVB-T2 demodulator tune setting. It returns -EINVAL if tnr_dmd is NULL, before any register access, and returns -EINVAL if clk_mode is not CXD2880_TNRDMD_CLOCKMODE_A, _B or _C (in the first clock-mode switch and again in each later clock-mode switch) or if bandwidth is not one of CXD2880_DTV_BW_8_MHZ, 7, 6, 5 or 1_7_MHZ; those -EINVAL returns happen after the earlier register writes have already been done and are not undone. Otherwise it writes a long fixed series of DMD-bank registers (constant init, TS-interface and clock-mode tables, with the TS-interface writes skipped when tnr_dmd->diver_mode is CXD2880_TNRDMD_DIVERMODE_SUB, then bandwidth- and clock-mode-specific tables, and an additional MRC table write only when diver_mode is CXD2880_TNRDMD_DIVERMODE_MAIN), and returns the first non-zero result from any register write at once, leaving the device partly configured. On success of all earlier steps it writes DMD register 0x00 = 0x00 and returns the result of writing DMD register 0xfd = 0x01, which is 0 or that write's error code.
note: Not a drop: slice 253-507 is the middle of x_tune_dvbt2_demod_setting (cxd2880_tnrdmd_dvbt2.c:23-746, slice cut the head, name was not shown). Real name used. I read the control flow (every return, every switch) of the 720-line function but not every register constant, so prose describes structure only. Prior 'dropped' was a mechanical decision; counted as wrong.

name: dib7000m_set_output_mode
prose: Precondition: state points to an initialized dib7000m_state (i2c_buffer_lock, i2c_adap, i2c_addr, reg_offs, revision and cfg usable) and mode is any int; OUTMODE_* values select cases, any other value takes the default case. Postcondition: it reads register 294+reg_offs through dib7000m_read_word (which returns 0 without any I2C access if the buffer lock acquisition is interrupted, and otherwise returns the two bytes in the read buffer even if i2c_transfer failed and only logged an error, so a failed transfer can yield stale buffer contents) and keeps its bit 4 as the start of smo_mode, with bit 1 set. By mode: GATED_CLK gives outreg 0x0400, CONT_CLK 0x0440, SERIAL 0x0482, DIVERSITY gives 0x0500 if cfg.hostbus_diversity is set and otherwise outreg 0 with 0x0c00 OR-ed into sram, FIFO gives outreg 0x0540, fifo_threshold 512 and smo_mode bits 1 and 2 set, HIGH_Z gives outreg 0; the default case leaves outreg 0, sram 0x0005 and fifo_threshold 1792. If cfg.output_mpeg2_in_188_bytes is set, bit 5 of smo_mode is set. It then writes smo_mode to register 294+reg_offs, fifo_threshold to 295+reg_offs, outreg to 1795 and sram to 1805 (reg_offs applies only to the first two), each through dib7000m_write_word, which returns -EINVAL without writing if the lock acquisition was interrupted, -EREMOTEIO if i2c_transfer did not complete one message, and 0 otherwise; all four writes are attempted regardless of earlier failures. If state->revision is 0x4003 it additionally reads register 909, clears bit 1, sets bit 1 again only when mode is OUTMODE_DIVERSITY, and writes it back, ignoring this write's result and the effect of a failed read. It returns the bitwise OR of the four write results (0 if all succeeded; with different failures the value is the OR of the error codes and not necessarily either one). Each read_word and write_word call takes i2c_buffer_lock only if the interruptible acquisition succeeds and releases it before returning; no lock is held on return.
note: Reviewers 1, 2, 3 all right (old prose missed: reg_offs only on 294/295 lines 195-198; stale buffer on i2c error line 98-101; lock acquisition can fail 80-83/111-114). dib7000m.c:151-207, helpers 76-131.

name: dib7000p_agc_startup
prose: Precondition: demod is a valid frontend whose demodulator_priv points to an initialized dib7000p_state, state->current_agc is valid for phases 1 to 4, and state->agc_state holds the current phase. Postcondition: it acts according to state->agc_state and returns either the delay in ms to wait before the next call or -1. Phase 0 sets the power mode, enables the ADC and clocks (via 0x79a/0x79b/0x780 writes if state->version is SOC7090, else dib7000p_set_adc_state and dib7000p_pll_clk_cfg), then returns -1 with the phase unchanged if dib7000p_set_agc_config fails or if dib7000p_set_dds returns a negative value (after the tuner's get_frequency callback has been used if it exists); otherwise it sets the phase to 1 and returns 7. Phase 1 calls cfg.agc_control(1) if set, writes register 78, then, if current_agc->perform_agc_softsplit is false, writes register 106, sets the phase to 2 and returns 5; if it is true, it sets the phase to 4 and returns 7; in both cases dib7000p_restart_agc is called. Phase 2 writes registers 75 and 106, sets the phase to 3 and returns 14. Phase 3 reads registers 396 and 394, writes registers 78, 75 and 106, restarts the AGC, sets the phase to 4 and returns 5. Phase 4 returns 5 and leaves the phase at 4 if dib7000p_update_lna returns non-zero, otherwise it sets the phase to 5 and returns 7. Phase 5 calls cfg.agc_control(0) if set, sets the phase to 6 and returns -1; this is the normal end of the startup sequence, not a failure. Any other phase value changes nothing and returns -1. Register read and write results are not checked.
note: Reviewers 2 and 3 right (phase 5 increments agc_state to 6, line 931; old prose said unchanged); reviewer 1 right (case 5 returns -1 without failure; case 4 may not advance when update_lna non-zero, 922-925). dib7000p.c:832-937.

name: hi_command
prose: Precondition: dev_addr identifies a reachable DRX device, cmd points to a valid drxj_hi_cmd, and result is a valid pointer (it is only written for commands that are not the SLEEP configuration). Postcondition: it first writes the command parameters to the HI RAM parameter registers according to cmd->cmd: CONFIG and ATOMIC_COPY write param6, param5, param4, param3, param2 and param1; BRDCTRL writes param2 and param1; NULL writes none; any other command value (including SIO_HI_RA_RAM_CMD_RESET) returns -EINVAL before anything is written. It then writes cmd->cmd to the HI command register. If the command is CONFIG with the sleep field of param5 equal to SLEEP_ZZZ (a power-down), it returns 0 without waiting and without writing *result. Otherwise it polls the command register until it reads 0, giving up with -ETIMEDOUT after DRXJ_MAX_RETRIES (100) polls, and then reads the HI result register into *result and returns 0. Any failing register read or write returns that error code at once. The command write is followed by msleep(1) only if cmd->cmd equals SIO_HI_RA_RAM_CMD_RESET, which the earlier switch rejects, so that sleep is not reached for any command that gets that far.
note: Slice cut the head: real function is hi_command (drxj.c:2266-2370), not an unnamed fragment, so FIX not drop. RESET is not a switch case (CMD_RESET=0x2, cases are CONFIG 0x3, BRDCTRL 0x7, NULL 0x0, ATOMIC_COPY), so the msleep at 2328 is dead. Previous 'dropped' decision counted as wrong. Read whole function.

name: set_agc_rf
prose: Precondition: demod points to an initialized demodulator whose my_common_attr, my_i2c_dev_addr and my_ext_attr are set, agc_settings points to a valid configuration, and atomic selects whether SCU registers are accessed through the atomic SCU accessors (true) or the plain DAP accessors (false). Postcondition: if ext_attr->standard equals agc_settings->standard, or both are QAM standards, or both are ATV standards, it programs the RF AGC registers according to agc_settings->ctrl_mode: AUTO enables the RF AGC DAC, sets the SCU AGC loop gain (2 for 8VSB, 5 for a QAM standard, 4 otherwise, taken from the current standard) and polarity, writes the speed reduction, writes the TOP value only if the matching IF AGC configuration (8VSB, QAM or ATV by agc_settings->standard) is in AUTO mode, and writes the cut-off current; USER enables the DAC, clears the SCU loop gain and writes the output level; OFF disables the DAC and the SCU loop. In that branch it returns -EINVAL for any other ctrl_mode, and in the AUTO case for an agc_settings->standard that is not 8VSB, QAM or ATV. If that branch is not taken (the standard is not currently active) no registers are written and ctrl_mode is not checked. It then stores *agc_settings into ext_attr->vsb_rf_agc_cfg when agc_settings->standard is 8VSB, or ext_attr->qam_rf_agc_cfg when it is ITU_A, ITU_B or ITU_C (the latter case only if DRXJ_VSB_ONLY is not defined), and returns 0; for any other standard it returns -EIO without storing. Any failing register read or write in the programming step returns that error code immediately, without storing the settings.
note: Reviewer 3 right: -EINVAL for a bad ctrl_mode only applies inside the standard-active branch (5082-5083); otherwise the code stores and returns 0 (5087-5103). Old prose also missed the atomic parameter and the -EIO / -EINVAL subtleties. drxj.c:4902-5106. 'name outside slice' mechanical note was about the slice only.

name: set_qam
prose: Precondition: demod, channel and the demod's my_i2c_dev_addr, my_ext_attr and my_common_attr are valid; tuner_freq_offset is passed through to set_frequency; op is a mask of QAM_SET_OP_ALL (0x1), QAM_SET_OP_CONSTELLATION (0x2) and QAM_SET_OP_SPECTRUM (0x4). Postcondition: if op has ALL or CONSTELLATION set it first derives the symbol-rate registers: for ext_attr->standard DRX_STANDARD_ITU_B it accepts only DRX_CONSTELLATION_QAM256 or QAM64 (any other value returns -EINVAL), uses a fixed iqm_rc_rate and overwrites channel->symbolrate with 5360537 or 5056941 respectively; for any other standard it returns -EIO if channel->symbolrate is 0, otherwise computes iqm_rc_rate and lc_symbol_freq (capped at 511) from sys_clock_freq and the symbol rate. It then selects the annex (A, B or C) from ext_attr->standard, returning -EINVAL for any other standard. These checks run before any register access. If op has ALL it then stops IQM_CF and sends the QAM DEMOD_RESET SCU command; if ALL or CONSTELLATION it sends SET_ENV and SET_PARAM SCU commands, writes IQM_RC_RATE_OFS, stores that value in ext_attr->iqm_rc_rate_ofs and calls set_qam_measurement; if ALL or SPECTRUM it calls set_frequency; it then writes the constellation-independent registers (symbol frequency, IQM stretch, and for ALL the LNA, sync and timeout registers, with a branch on ITU_B versus a switch over channel->constellation where QAM16/64/256 and QAM32/128 take different writes and any other constellation returns -EIO); if ALL or CONSTELLATION it writes the IQM filter taps for the standard (for ITU_B only QAM64 and QAM256 are accepted, else -EIO) and the constellation-specific registers (QAM16, 32, 64, 128 and 256 accepted, any other value returns -EIO); if ALL it sets MPEG TEI handling, bit reversal and start width and enables the MPEG output through ctrl_set_cfg_mpeg_output using a copy of common_attr->mpeg_cfg; if ALL or CONSTELLATION it sends the DEMOD_START SCU command. Whatever op is, it finally writes ACTIVE to IQM_COMM_EXEC, QAM_COMM_EXEC and FEC_COMM_EXEC and returns 0. Any failing register access, SCU command or called helper returns its error code at once, leaving the earlier writes in place. No locks or references are taken in this function.
note: Slice cut the head and the packet name was wrong: real function is set_qam (drxj.c:7845-8659), op flags defined at 7834-7836. Read the structure (every return, switch and op-flag block, 7990-8660) and the key blocks, but I did not read every register constant or every SCU parameter. Old prose was correct in outline (mechanical reviewer right about the name) but missed -EIO returns and the unconditional final COMM_EXEC writes. Large function read partly.

name: set_qam_channel
prose: Precondition: demod and channel are valid pointers, and ext_attr is demod->my_ext_attr. Postcondition: it returns -EINVAL, before any register access or state change, for channel->constellation of QAM16, QAM32, QAM128 or any value not named below, for QAM64 or QAM256 when ext_attr->standard is not DRX_STANDARD_ITU_B, and for DRX_CONSTELLATION_AUTO when the standard is neither ITU_B nor ITU_C. For QAM64 or QAM256 with ITU_B it sets ext_attr->constellation to the requested one and ext_attr->mirror to DRX_MIRROR_NO if channel->mirror is DRX_MIRROR_AUTO (otherwise to channel->mirror), calls set_qam with QAM_SET_OP_ALL and then qam64auto or qam256auto; channel->constellation is not changed. For DRX_CONSTELLATION_AUTO with ITU_B it sets channel->constellation and ext_attr->constellation to QAM256 (mirror as above), runs set_qam and qam256auto, and if the resulting local lock status is at least DRX_LOCKED it sets channel->constellation back to DRX_CONSTELLATION_AUTO and returns 0; otherwise it switches both to QAM64, adjusts SCU_RAM_QAM_CTL_ENA and the QAM FSM state target, runs set_qam with QAM_SET_OP_CONSTELLATION, restores the control-enable register, runs qam64auto, restores channel->constellation to DRX_CONSTELLATION_AUTO and returns 0. For AUTO with ITU_C it sets QAM64, forces rate hunting through the same two SCU registers, runs set_qam with QAM_SET_OP_CONSTELLATION, restores the register, runs qam64auto, restores channel->constellation to DRX_CONSTELLATION_AUTO and returns 0. On any failing helper or register access it returns that negative error code at once, leaving the demodulator partly programmed; on the AUTO paths the error exit also restores channel->constellation to DRX_CONSTELLATION_AUTO (the auto flag is set before the first helper call), while ext_attr->constellation and ext_attr->mirror stay at the last attempted values. The local lock status is never returned, so a 0 return does not mean a carrier lock was found, and the QAM64 step after a failed QAM256 attempt, as well as the ITU_C path, does not test whether lock was obtained.
note: Reviewer 1 right (success is not lock; lock_status local). Reviewers 2 and 3 WRONG: the rw_error label restores channel->constellation to DRX_CONSTELLATION_AUTO when auto_flag is set (drxj.c rw_error at about 9272-9276: 'if (auto_flag) channel->constellation = DRX_CONSTELLATION_AUTO'), and auto_flag is set before any helper call in both AUTO paths (ITU_B first statement; ITU_C right after the constellation assignment). set_qam_channel at 9087-9276.

name: DRX_Start
prose: Precondition: state points to a valid drxd_state; off is a frequency offset that the function first rounds to the nearest multiple of 1000 and divides by 1000. Postcondition: if state->drxd_state is not DRXD_STOPPED it returns -1 before touching the hardware or any state. Otherwise it resets with ResetECOD and then runs InitSC alone when state->type_A is true, or InitFT, InitCP, InitCE, InitEQ and InitSC in that order when it is false, restores the IF and RF AGC configurations (SetCfgIfAgc, SetCfgRfAgc), and builds the transmission parameters and operation mode from props.transmission_mode, guard_interval, hierarchy, modulation and code_rate_HP (unset or unknown values select the automatic-detection bits and a first guess), writing the matching EC/EQ registers only when state->type_A is true. It sets props.bandwidth_hz to 8000000 if it was 0, and returns -EINVAL if it is not 0, 6000000, 7000000 or 8000000, after the earlier initialisation has already been done and not undone. It then writes the bandwidth-dependent registers, enables or disables slave mode in SC_RA_RAM_CONFIG (enabled only for 2K mode with a 1/32 guard interval), calls SetCfgNoiseCalibration, and, if state->cscd_state is CSCD_INIT, writes the sample-rate scan register and sets state->cscd_state to CSCD_SET. It writes the FE_IF_REG_INCR registers, calls SetFrequencyShift (which updates state->fe_fs_add_incr and state->org_fe_fs_add_incr and writes the shift register; its return value is ignored), starts the SC (SC_COMM_STATE, SC_COMM_EXEC), sends SC_SetPrefParamCommand with an operation mode that is overwritten with all five auto-detect bits set (the earlier operationMode value is discarded), starts the lock/track process, calls StartOC and, if state->operation_mode is not OM_Default, StartDiversity. Only if every step succeeds does it set state->drxd_state to DRXD_STARTED (not DRXD_ACTIVE). The return value is 0, or the first negative status of a checked step, with all later steps skipped and the device left partly configured; failures of SetFrequencyShift are not reported, and a failed transmission-mode register write on a type_A device is not checked separately and can be overwritten by the later hierarchy writes. Register read and write results of the steps listed are returned through the same status.
note: Reviewer 1 right (type_A path only ResetECOD+InitSC; old prose already had it); reviewer 2 right: drxd_state is set, but to DRXD_STARTED (line 2415), and the old prose wrongly said DRXD_ACTIVE; reviewer 3 right (SetFrequencyShift result ignored, line 2376). Also found: operationMode overwritten at 2390 (#if 1); early transmission_mode write status can be masked on type_A (no status check after the switch at 1957-1983). drxd_hard.c:1888-2419 read fully.

name: switch_antenna_to_qam
prose: Precondition: state points to a valid drxk_state whose antenna_gpio, antenna_dvbt and m_gpio fields have been set up. Postcondition: if state->antenna_gpio is 0 it returns 0 without any change. Otherwise it takes the antenna bits of state->m_gpio as a boolean (non-zero or zero) and, only if that boolean differs from state->antenna_dvbt, it changes state->m_gpio by clearing the state->antenna_gpio bits when state->antenna_dvbt is true or setting them when it is false, and calls write_gpio(state) and uses its result; if the boolean already equals state->antenna_dvbt nothing is changed and the result is 0. If the result is negative it logs the error with pr_err. It returns that result, 0 or the negative error from write_gpio; state->m_gpio keeps the new value even if write_gpio fails. It takes no locks and no references.
note: Slice/name mismatch: the packet name switch_antenna_to_dvbc does not exist; the code is switch_antenna_to_qam (drxk_hard.c:5910-5933). Its sibling switch_antenna_to_dvbt (5935-5958) has the inverted condition. Old prose matched the code; mechanical reviewer right only about the name.

name: m88ds3103_set_frontend
prose: Precondition: fe->demodulator_priv points to an initialized m88ds3103_dev (regmap, client and cfg valid, chip_id and chiptype set) and fe->dtv_property_cache holds the requested delivery_system, frequency and symbol_rate. Postcondition: if dev->warm is false it returns -EAGAIN before any hardware access. Otherwise it resets the demodulator, optionally disables the clock path (M88RS6000 chips), calls the tuner set_params and get_frequency callbacks if present (a non-zero result is returned at once; without get_frequency the nominal frequency is used), sets dev->mclk and programs the main and TS clocks, and then writes the init table for the requested delivery system only when it differs from dev->delivery_system. It returns -EINVAL for a delivery_system that is neither SYS_DVBS nor SYS_DVBS2 and for a cfg->ts_mode that is not one of M88DS3103_TS_SERIAL, SERIAL_D7, PARALLEL or CI; these checks happen after the earlier register writes and tuner calls, which are not undone. It then programs the TS mode, clock divider, symbol rate, spectrum inversion, AGC and carrier offset registers and releases the demodulator, and on reaching the end sets dev->delivery_system to the requested value and returns 0. Any failing regmap access, update_bits or tuner callback (non-zero ret) is returned immediately with dev->delivery_system unchanged, although dev->mclk and many registers may already have been modified. For chiptype M88DS3103_CHIPTYPE_3103B the results of m88ds3103b_select_mclk, m88ds3103b_set_mclk, m88ds3103b_dt_read, m88ds3103b_dt_write and the regmap_read/regmap_write at register 0x30 are not checked, so a 0 return does not prove those writes succeeded. No locks or references are taken in this function.
note: Reviewer 4 right: results of m88ds3103b_select_mclk/set_mclk/dt_write/dt_read and the 0x30 regmap access are ignored (m88ds3103.c lines 703-704, 820-842, 934). Old prose also implied -EINVAL happens without hardware changes; they come after writes (lines 735-737, 789-792, 875-878). The tuner callbacks' results are returned. Slice cut the head only (function at 618-1016). Read fully.

name: or51132_set_parameters
prose: Precondition: fe is a valid dvb_frontend whose demodulator_priv points to a valid or51132_state; when a firmware upload is needed, state->i2c->dev.parent and state->config->set_ts_params are valid. Postcondition: if the firmware class (VSB for VSB_8, QAM for QAM_AUTO, QAM_64 or QAM_256, unknown otherwise) of p->modulation differs from that of state->current_modulation, it chooses the VSB or QAM firmware and returns -1 if the class of p->modulation is unknown; otherwise it calls request_firmware (returning its error if it fails, with nothing changed), calls or51132_load_firmware, calls release_firmware (returning the load error if the load failed), and then calls state->config->set_ts_params(fe, 0 for VSB or 1 for QAM) and ignores its result. On those three failure returns state->current_modulation and state->current_frequency are unchanged. If state->current_modulation differs from p->modulation it then sets it to p->modulation and calls or51132_setmode(fe) with the result ignored. If fe->ops.tuner_ops.set_params exists it calls it (result ignored) and, only inside that case, calls fe->ops.i2c_gate_ctrl(fe, 0) when that hook exists. It then calls or51132_setmode(fe) again (result ignored), sets state->current_frequency to p->frequency and returns 0, so a 0 return does not prove the tuner or the mode programming succeeded.
note: Reviewer 1 right (setmode result ignored, 345 and 354); reviewer 3 right (i2c_gate_ctrl is called only inside the tuner set_params if-block, 348-351; old prose read as independent). or51132.c:294-359.

name: rtl2830_regmap_gather_write
prose: Precondition: context is the struct i2c_client of the device; reg points to at least one byte (only the first register byte is used and reg_len is not used); val points to val_len bytes with val_len at most 255 (the local buffer buf[256] holds one register byte plus the value, and there is no length check); the caller must hold the adapter lock because __i2c_transfer, which does not lock, is used. Postcondition: it copies the first byte of reg and then val_len bytes of val into a local buffer and sends them as one I2C write message of 1 + val_len bytes to client->addr. It returns 0 if exactly one message was transferred. Otherwise it logs a warning with dev_warn and returns the negative error from __i2c_transfer, or -EREMOTEIO if __i2c_transfer returned 0 or any other non-negative count different from 1. No memory is allocated or freed and no references are taken.
note: Not a drop: the slice 761-898 starts in the middle of rtl2830_regmap_gather_write (defined at rtl2830.c:742-770; slice cut the head); real name used. Old prose described the tail correctly but omitted the buf[256] limit and that the lock is the caller's. The old 'dropped' decision counted as wrong.

name: si2168_set_frontend
prose: Precondition: fe->demodulator_priv is the si2168 i2c_client, i2c_get_clientdata(client) returns its si2168_dev, and fe->dtv_property_cache holds the requested delivery_system, bandwidth_hz, stream_id and symbol_rate. Postcondition: it returns -EAGAIN without touching the hardware if dev->active is false; -EINVAL if c->delivery_system is not SYS_DVBT, SYS_DVBC_ANNEX_A or SYS_DVBT2, and -EINVAL if c->bandwidth_hz is 0, in both cases before the tuner is programmed. Otherwise it maps the bandwidth to a code (up to 2, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 or 10 MHz, else 0x0f), calls fe->ops.tuner_ops.set_params if it is set (returning a non-zero result at once), and then sends a fixed sequence of si2168 commands with si2168_cmd_execute, including a PLP selection command only for SYS_DVBT2, the DVB-C symbol rate (symbol_rate / 1000) only for SYS_DVBC_ANNEX_A, and the delivery-system/bandwidth word with the spectral-inversion bit from dev->spectral_inversion and the TS clock polarity from dev->ts_clock_inv. A non-zero result from any command is returned immediately, leaving the chip partly programmed. After the last command succeeds it sets dev->delivery_system to c->delivery_system, calls si2168_ts_bus_ctrl(fe, 1), and returns 0 if that succeeds or its non-zero result otherwise; in that last failure dev->delivery_system has already been updated. No locks or references are taken in this function.
note: Slice name wrong: packet says si2168_set_params, real function is si2168_set_frontend (si2168.c:230-406; slice cut the head). Old prose missed the -EAGAIN return (dev->active false, 245-248) and -EINVAL for unsupported delivery systems (260-262), and that dev->delivery_system is set before the ts_bus_ctrl that may still fail (395-400). Mechanical reviewer right about the name.

name: stb0899_dvbs_algo
prose: Precondition: state is a valid initialised stb0899_state whose params hold the requested frequency and symbol rate and whose internal fields (master_clk, mclk, derot_percent, t_agc1, t_agc2, freq and so on) are populated and whose config is valid. This is the DVB-S search; it calls stb0899_first_subrange itself, so no earlier call is required. Postcondition: it sets internal->direction to 1, programs the symbol rate and the carrier loop registers according to params->srate, sets the timing loop to acquisition, computes internal->derot_step, t_derot and t_data, puts the stream merger in reset, configures the demapper and equalizer registers, calls stb0899_first_subrange and then repeats the following until internal->status is RANGEOK or internal->sub_range becomes 0: reset the derotator, set internal->derot_freq to 0 and internal->status to NOAGC1, enable the tuner I2C gate, call the config's tuner_set_frequency and tuner_get_frequency if present (the latter can overwrite internal->freq), sleep t_agc1 + t_agc2 + t_derot ms, set status to AGC1OK, read the tuner bandwidth if the callback exists, disable the tuner I2C gate, run stb0899_search_tmg (if params->srate <= bandwidth / 2) or stb0899_check_tmg, and, only while the status stays TIMINGOK, run the carrier search, then the data search, then the range check; when all of those succeed with RANGEOK it sets internal->freq to params->freq minus the derotator offset scaled by mclk and reads internal->fecrate from the PLPARM register. If the status is not RANGEOK at the end of an iteration it calls next_sub_range. After the loop it always programs the tracking values RTC 0x33 and CFD 0xf7. Only when the status is RANGEOK does it also write EQON and VITSYNC, program DEMAPVIT and BCLC for the detected puncture rate (FEC 6/7 writes ACLC 0x88 and BCLC 0x9a; an unsupported rate writes nothing and only logs), release the stream-merger reset, disable the carrier detector and read the equalizer coefficients into a local array. It returns internal->status, which is RANGEOK on success and otherwise whatever status the last search step left; in the failing case the stream merger stays in reset, the carrier detector stays enabled and internal->fecrate is not updated. The tuner I2C gate is disabled on return. Register access errors are not checked.
note: Slice name wrong: packet says stb0899_search_dvbs, real function is stb0899_dvbs_algo (stb0899_algo.c:489-~730). Reviewer 3 right: stb0899_first_subrange is called inside (line 577), not required beforehand. Old prose's 'TIMINGNOK, CARRIERNOK, DATANOK or RANGENOK' list is not established by this function (the values are set inside the callee search functions), removed. Read fully, but not the callees' internals.

name: stb0899_read_snr
prose: Precondition: fe->demodulator_priv points to a valid stb0899_state with state->delsys set, and snr points to a writable u16. Postcondition: it sets *snr to 0, reads the VSTATUS register, and branches on state->delsys. For SYS_DVBS and SYS_DSS, if internal->lock is set and the VSTATUS Viterbi-locked field is non-zero, it reads the two NIR registers and sets *snr to the value from stb0899_table_lookup on the C/N table (units of 0.1 dB); otherwise *snr stays 0. For SYS_DVBS2, if internal->lock is set it reads the ESN0 quantisation (UWP_CNTRL1) and estimate (UWP_STAT2) fields and sets *snr to 301 if the estimate field is 1, 270 if it is 2, and otherwise to (quantn - estn) / 10 using the quant and est table lookups; that difference is computed in unsigned int arithmetic, so a negative difference wraps and the u16 store keeps only the low 16 bits, i.e. it is not stored as a negative number. If internal->lock is clear, *snr stays 0. For any other delivery system it returns -EINVAL with *snr equal to 0. In every other case it returns 0, including when *snr was left at 0 because the demodulator is not locked. Register access errors are not checked and no locks or references are taken.
note: Reviewer right: val is unsigned int and *snr is u16 (stb0899_drv.c:997, 1034-1036), so a negative difference wraps rather than being negative. Old prose also omitted the VSTATUS_LOCKEDVIT condition on the DVB-S path (1007) and the unconditional VSTATUS read (1002). Name was right in the packet label despite 'truncated' (function at 992-1047; slice cut the head).

name: stb0899_set_delivery
prose: Precondition: state points to a valid stb0899_state whose delsys field selects the delivery system; register read and write results are not checked. Postcondition: it first reads STOPCLK1 and STOPCLK2 into a local two-byte array and then, according to state->delsys, writes other registers and modifies that array. SYS_DVBS: FECM gets RSVD0 = 0 and VITERBI_ON = 1; RSULC = 0xb1, TSULC = 0x40, RSLLC = 0x42, TSLPL = 0x12; TSTRES gets FRESLDPC = 1; in the array CHK8PSK, CKFEC108, CKFEC216, CKPKDLIN108, CKPKDLIN216, CKINTBUF216 and CKS2DMD108 are set to 1 and CKCORE216 to 0. SYS_DVBS2: FECM gets RSVD0 = 0 and VITERBI_ON = 0; RSULC = 0xb1, TSULC = 0x42, RSLLC = 0x40, TSLPL = 0x02; TSTRES gets FRESLDPC = 0; in the array CHK8PSK is set to 1 and CKFEC108, CKFEC216, CKPKDLIN108, CKPKDLIN216, CKINTBUF216, CKCORE216 and CKS2DMD108 are set to 0. SYS_DSS: FECM gets RSVD0 = 1 and VITERBI_ON = 1; RSULC = 0xa1, TSULC = 0x61, RSLLC = 0x42 (TSLPL is not written); TSTRES gets FRESLDPC = 1; in the array CHK8PSK, CKFEC108, CKFEC216, CKPKDLIN108, CKPKDLIN216 and CKS2DMD108 are set to 1 and CKCORE216 to 0, and CKINTBUF216 is left as read. Any other delsys only logs an error and changes no register in the switch. For every delsys value, including the unsupported ones, it then clears CKADCI108 in the first array byte and writes both bytes back to STOPCLK1 with one stb0899_write_regs call. The function returns nothing and takes no locks.
note: Reviewer 3 right: in the SYS_DVBS2 case CKS2DMD108 is set to 0 (stb0899_drv.c:1354), the old prose said 1. Reviewer 1 right (STOPCLK written for unsupported delsys, 1386-1387; old prose had it). Reviewer 2 wrong against the revised prose: DSS indeed omits TSLPL and writes TSTRES (1356-1381), and the old prose already said so. stb0899_drv.c:1290-1388.

name: stv0900_get_optim_carr_loop
prose: Precondition: srate, modcode, pilot and chip_id hold values of their declared types; the function only reads its parameters and static const tables, takes no locks and allocates nothing. Postcondition: it returns a u8 ACLC carrier-loop value, defaulting to 0x29. It chooses three tables from chip_id in three cases: for chip_id <= 0x12 it uses FE_STV0900_S2CarLoop (normal), FE_STV0900_S2LowQPCarLoopCut30 (low QPSK) and FE_STV0900_S2APSKCarLoopCut30 (APSK); for chip_id == 0x20 the Cut20 versions of the three; for any other chip_id (above 0x12 and not 0x20) FE_STV0900_S2CarLoopCut30, FE_STV0900_S2LowQPCarLoopCut30 and FE_STV0900_S2APSKCarLoopCut30; cllas2_size is the ARRAY_SIZE of the APSK table chosen. It then computes an index i: if modcode < STV0900_QPSK_12 it scans the first 3 entries of the low-QPSK table for modcode and uses i = 2 if none matches; otherwise it scans the first 14 entries of the normal table, and if none matches it scans the first 11 entries of the APSK table and uses i = 10 if still not found. It returns the table entry cllqs2[i] when modcode <= STV0900_QPSK_25, or cls2[i] when modcode <= STV0900_8PSK_910, in both cases chosen by pilot (non-zero selects the pilots-on field) and by srate bucket (<= 3000000, <= 7000000, <= 15000000, <= 25000000, otherwise the highest bucket); for larger modcode values, if i < cllas2_size it returns cllas2[i] pilots-on value for the same srate buckets (pilot is ignored), otherwise it returns 0x29.
note: Reviewer 4 right: the old prose put the 'otherwise' (chip_id > 0x12 and != 0x20) case on FE_STV0900_S2CarLoop; the code uses FE_STV0900_S2CarLoopCut30 for it (1091-1095) and FE_STV0900_S2CarLoop only for chip_id <= 0x12 (1081-1085). Reviewer 3 right (<= 0x12 uses Cut30 low-QP/APSK tables, 1083-1085). Contracts left empty: tables are global const data. stv0900_core.c:1072-1184.

name: stv0900_get_rf_level
prose: Precondition: intp points to an initialized stv0900_internal and lookup is NULL or a table whose regval entries are monotonic from table[0] to table[size-1] (either increasing or decreasing); if size is 1 the AGC gain read must not equal table[0].regval, and no two bracketing entries may have equal regval, since the interpolation divides by their difference. Postcondition: it returns 0 if lookup is NULL or lookup->size <= 0. Otherwise it reads the 16-bit AGC gain from the AGCIQ_VALUE1/AGCIQ_VALUE0 bit fields. If the gain lies between table[0].regval and table[size-1].regval inclusive (in either ordering, as the INRANGE macro accepts both), it narrows to a bracketing pair of entries by bisection and returns the realval obtained by linear interpolation between them (integer arithmetic, truncated). If the gain is outside that interval it returns 5 if the gain is greater than table[0].regval, else -100 if the gain is less than table[size-1].regval; if neither comparison holds (possible only when the endpoints are ordered so that neither is true) it returns 0. If size is 1 and the gain equals table[0].regval it divides by zero. No locks are taken and nothing is allocated or retained.
note: Reviewers 1 and 4 right: the outside-range branches compare against table[0] (gain > table[0].regval gives 5) and table[size-1] (gain < table[size-1].regval gives -100), stv0900_core.c:629-632, and the old prose had the endpoints inverted. Reviewer 3 right: size==1 with gain==regval[0] divides by zero (626-627). Reviewer 2 (a reasoning about -100/5 being reversed) is about the same lines and also right. INRANGE (stv0900_priv.h:17) accepts either ordering, so 'strictly increasing' in the old prose was wrong. Function at 590-637, slice cut the head.

name: tc90522s_get_frontend
prose: Precondition: fe->demodulator_priv points to a valid tc90522_state with a usable I2C client, and c points to the frontend's dtv_frontend_properties. Postcondition: it always returns 0; I2C read failures are not reported. It sets c->delivery_system to SYS_ISDBS and c->symbol_rate to 28860000. It reads 5 bytes from register 0xe6 (a layer count of 0 is kept if that read fails); if the read succeeds it sets c->stream_id, c->modulation (PSK_8 if the high-layer code is 7, else QPSK), c->fec_inner, the layer[0] and layer[1] fec, modulation and segment_count fields, and a layer count of 1, or 2 if the low-layer code is non-zero; if it fails those fields are left as they were. It sets c->strength.len to 0 and, if the tuner has get_rf_strength, calls it and ignores the result. It sets c->cnr.len to 1 and c->cnr.stat[0].scale to FE_SCALE_NOT_AVAILABLE, reads 2 bytes from register 0xbc, and only if that read succeeds and the value is at least 3000 computes the C/N and sets stat[0].svalue and scale FE_SCALE_DECIBEL. It then zeroes the whole c->post_bit_error and c->post_bit_count structures with memset, sets their len to the layer count, reads 10 bytes from register 0xeb once, and for each of the layers entries sets scale to FE_SCALE_NOT_AVAILABLE if that read failed, or FE_SCALE_COUNTER with uvalue taken from the bytes of that layer (the error count for post_bit_error, and the bit count scaled by 204 * 8 for post_bit_count) if it succeeded. No locks or references are taken.
note: Reviewer 1 right (errors ignored, always 0). Reviewer 3 wrong: both post_bit_error and post_bit_count are memset to zero (tc90522.c:283 and 297) before len and entries are set. Function at 195-312, slice 1-260 cut the tail but I read the full function.

name: cmp_establish_pp_connection
prose: Precondition: fdtv points to an initialized firedtv device, plug is a non-negative output plug index (the register address is CMP_OUTPUT_PLUG_CONTROL_REG_0 + (plug << 2)), and channel is the isochronous channel to use. Postcondition: it reads the output plug control register with cmp_read and returns that negative error at once if the read fails (cmp_read logs the I/O error). It then loops: if the plug is not online it logs and returns -EBUSY; if the register already has a non-zero p2p connection count and its channel differs from channel it logs and returns -EBUSY; if the count is non-zero and the channel matches it logs an overlay message and does not change the channel fields; if the count is zero it sets the channel to channel, the data rate to S400 and the overhead id to 0 in the new value. It increments the p2p connection count in the new value and issues a compare-and-swap with cmp_lock (returning its negative error at once if it fails; cmp_lock logs the I/O error). If the value returned in opcr[0] differs from the expected old value, the swap is not considered committed and the loop repeats with the value returned, for at most 6 swap attempts in total; after the sixth mismatch it returns -EBUSY without logging. If the value matches it returns 0. No isochronous channel or bandwidth is allocated at the IRM, and no locks are held by this function.
note: Reviewer 3 right: the final -EBUSY after 6 failed compare-and-swap attempts (firedtv-avc.c:1431-1433) has no log message, only the offline and channel-change -EBUSY returns log; reviewer 1 right (cmp_read/cmp_lock negative errno returned, covered in prior prose). cmp_establish_pp_connection at 1379-1437.

name: adv7511_csc_coeff
prose: Precondition: sd is an initialized adv7511 subdev whose main register map is reachable over I2C (through adv7511_rd and adv7511_wr), and A1-A4, B1-B4, C1-C4 are 16-bit CSC coefficients. Postcondition: for each of the twelve coefficients it writes the low byte (bits 0-7) of the coefficient to registers 0x19, 0x1B, 0x1D, 0x1F (A1-A4), 0x21, 0x23, 0x25, 0x27 (B1-B4) and 0x29, 0x2B, 0x2D, 0x2F (C1-C4), and updates registers 0x18, 0x1A, 0x1C, 0x1E, 0x20, 0x22, 0x24, 0x26, 0x28, 0x2A, 0x2C and 0x2E with the new value (old & 0xe0) | (coefficient >> 8 truncated to 8 bits): the old top three bits of the register are kept and ORed with bits 13-15 of the coefficient, and the low five bits become coefficient bits 8-12 (their old contents are cleared). Each register update is a read followed by a write; each write is tried up to three times, with an error message if it still fails, and failures are not reported to the caller. The order is the high-byte register followed by the low-byte register for each coefficient, A1 first and C4 last. The function returns nothing and takes no locks.
note: Reviewers 1, 2 and 4 right: coefficient>>8 is not masked, so its bits 5-7 (coefficient bits 13-15) are ORed into the preserved top three bits, and the low five register bits get coefficient bits 8-12, not bits 0-4 (adv7511-v4l2.c:291-318, wr_and_or at 209-211). adv7511_wr retries 3 times (198-203).

name: alvium_write_hshake
prose: Precondition: alvium points to a valid, initialized alvium_dev and reg is a register of the device (addresses with the REG_BCRM_V4L2 flag are offset by alvium->bcrm_addr). Postcondition: it uses a sticky error variable ret that starts at 0 and is passed to alvium_write and alvium_read; once ret is non-zero, later alvium_write calls do nothing and return it, and later alvium_read calls return it after setting *val to 0. It writes 0 to the write-handshake register and then writes val to reg; if ret is non-zero after these two (the first write's error is kept, because the second write is skipped), it logs and returns that error. It then runs read_poll_timeout on the handshake register with a condition that the handshake bit0 equals 1, with 15 ms sleep intervals and a 45 ms timeout. However, read_poll_timeout assigns the return value of alvium_read (0 on success, since the register value is written through the pointer and then overwritten) to hshake_bit, and the macro's own timeout result is discarded, so after a successful read the condition (bit0 == 1) is never true and the loop ends only at the 45 ms timeout without setting ret; only a failing register read sets ret, which is then logged and returned. It then writes 0 to the handshake register (returning ret with a log if that fails) and runs a second poll with the condition bit0 equal to 0 which, for the same reason, is satisfied by the first successful read (after a first sleep of the minimum interval); a failed read sets ret, which is logged and returned. It returns 0 if no step set ret. It therefore does not itself confirm that the device set and cleared the handshake bit; the handshake wait is effectively a delay of about 45 ms plus the sleep of the second poll, and a handshake timeout is not reported.
note: Reviewers 2 right (initial reset write error preserved: cci_write returns *err without writing when *err is set, v4l2-cci.c:99-100, so the second write is skipped); reviewers 1 and 3 wrong ('overwritten by the next write'). New finding the old prose missed: read_poll_timeout(op,val,...) does (val)=op(args) (iopoll.h:145), storing alvium_read's return code (0) into hshake_bit, so the bit0 conditions at alvium-csi2.c:356 and :374 never test the register; and the macro's -ETIMEDOUT result is not used. alvium_write_hshake at 340-384.

name: alvium_get_bcrm_vers
prose: Precondition: alvium points to a valid, initialized alvium_dev. Postcondition: it reads the BCRM minor version and then the major version through alvium_read with a shared error variable ret that starts at 0; if the minor read fails, ret holds that error, the major read is skipped (alvium_read returns the existing error after setting the value to 0), and the function returns the minor-read error; if only the major read fails it returns the major-read error. If both succeed it logs the bcrm version (minor then major, printed as min.maj) with dev_info and returns 0. It takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: Reviewer 2 right; reviewers 1 and 3 wrong: because ret is also passed as the err pointer, cci_read returns *err immediately when it is already set (v4l2-cci.c:35-36), so the first error is preserved and not overwritten by the second read (alvium-csi2.c:392-395). Note the log prints min then max as 'min.maj', i.e. minor first, as written in the code (397).

name: ccs_read_frame_fmt
prose: Precondition: sensor is a valid CCS sensor whose limits for the frame format model type, subtype and descriptor (FRAME_FORMAT_DESCRIPTOR or FRAME_FORMAT_DESCRIPTOR_4) are readable through CCS_LIM and CCS_LIM_AT, and sensor->src->sd has a valid subdevdata. Postcondition: it reads the model type and subtype, derives the number of column descriptors and row descriptors from the subtype, and walks all ncol_desc + nrow_desc descriptors in order. For each descriptor it extracts the pixel code and pixel count using the 2-byte layout if the model type is CCS_FRAME_FORMAT_MODEL_TYPE_2_BYTE or the 4-byte layout if it is CCS_FRAME_FORMAT_MODEL_TYPE_4_BYTE; for any other model type it returns -EINVAL when it reaches the first descriptor, leaving sensor fields untouched by it but (when i is above 0 it cannot happen, since the type is the same for all descriptors) so in practice -EINVAL happens at the first descriptor, before any sensor field is changed. If there are no descriptors at all the loop does not run and the type is not checked. For column descriptors it sets sensor->visible_pixel_start to the running pixel_count whenever the pixel code is visible-pixel and adds the pixel count to pixel_count. For row descriptors, an embedded row group sets sensor->embedded_start to the running line_count and sensor->embedded_end to line_count plus the pixel count only if sensor->embedded_end is still 0 (so it keeps a value left by an earlier call, and only the first embedded row group is recorded); a visible-pixel row group sets sensor->image_start to the running line_count, so the last visible group wins; line_count then grows by the pixel count. After the loop, if sensor->embedded_end is greater than sensor->image_start it sets sensor->image_start to sensor->embedded_end. It returns 0 in all cases other than the -EINVAL above. Nothing is allocated and no locks or references are taken.
note: Slice cut the head and the packet name was wrong: real function is ccs_read_frame_fmt (ccs-core.c:247-372). Old prose imprecise: embedded fields are only set while sensor->embedded_end is 0 (line 347-350) so earlier values survive; the -EINVAL occurs at the first descriptor and only if there is at least one descriptor. Mechanical reviewer right about the name.

name: imx214_set_ctrl
prose: Precondition: ctrl belongs to the imx214 control handler (ctrl->handler is &imx214->ctrls), the active subdev state is available for the VBLANK case, and for a handled control id the sensor's imx214->hflip and imx214->vflip controls exist. Postcondition: if ctrl->id is V4L2_CID_VBLANK it first reads the active state's format for pad 0 and updates the exposure control's range (maximum format->height + value - IMX214_EXPOSURE_OFFSET, default the smaller of that and IMX214_EXPOSURE_DEFAULT) with __v4l2_ctrl_modify_range, ignoring its result. It then calls pm_runtime_get_if_in_use; if that returns 0 (device not in use) it returns 0 at once for every control id, including ids the function does not handle, without writing any register and without a runtime PM reference to release (a negative return from pm_runtime_get_if_in_use is not tested, so the function carries on and still calls pm_runtime_put). Otherwise it switches on ctrl->id: analogue gain is written to ANALOG_GAIN and SHORT_ANALOG_GAIN, digital gain goes through imx214_update_digital_gain, exposure to EXPOSURE, hflip or vflip writes ORIENTATION as hflip->val | vflip->val << 1, vblank writes FRM_LENGTH_LINES as format->height + value, test pattern writes imx214_test_pattern_val[ctrl->val] to TEST_PATTERN, and the red, green-red, blue and green-blue pattern controls write ctrl->val to their registers; any other id sets ret to -EINVAL. It always calls pm_runtime_put on this path and returns ret, which is 0 on success, -EINVAL for an unhandled id, or the first error stored by cci_write (cci_write skips its write and keeps the stored error once ret is non-zero, so later writes do not replace it).
note: Reviewer 1 right (unhandled id returns 0 when device is not in use, line 826-827, since the pm check precedes the switch); reviewer 2 right (cci_write keeps the first error); reviewer 3 right (TEST_PATTERN writes imx214_test_pattern_val[ctrl->val], line 853, not ctrl->val). Extra: pm_runtime_get_if_in_use can return a negative value, which !x does not catch. imx214.c:798-878.

name: msp3400c_set_audmode
prose: Precondition: client is a valid i2c_client whose client data leads to an msp_state, and state->audmode, state->mode, state->opmode, state->rxsubchans and state->nicam_on hold their current values. Postcondition: if state->opmode is OPMODE_AUTOSELECT it logs a debug message and returns without any hardware access. Otherwise, unless state->mode is MSP_MODE_EXTERN, it computes an effective audmode from state->audmode and state->rxsubchans: mono only becomes V4L2_TUNER_MODE_MONO; if LANG2 is present, MONO or STEREO becomes LANG1; otherwise any non-mono audmode becomes STEREO. It then acts on state->mode: FM_TERRA writes DSP register 0x000e (0x3001 for stereo, 0x3000 for the other modes); FM_SAT sets the sound carriers with msp3400c_set_carrier according to the audmode; NICAM1, NICAM2 and AM_NICAM set the source word to 0x0100 if state->nicam_on; EXTERN sets it to 0x0200; BTSC and FM_RADIO change nothing here; any other state->mode returns without writing anything or calling msp_set_source. It then adjusts the source word: STEREO and LANG1_LANG2 OR in 0x0020, LANG2 ORs in 0x0010, LANG1 adds nothing, and MONO, when state->mode is AM_NICAM, calls msp_set_scart(client, SCART_MONO, 0) and sets the source to 0x0200, while for other modes with MONO it replaces the source by 0x0030 if rxsubchans includes V4L2_TUNER_SUB_STEREO. It finally calls msp_set_source(client, source word). It returns nothing, takes no locks and does not call msp3400c_detect_stereo.
note: Reviewer wrong for this function: the OPMODE_AUTOSELECT check returns immediately (msp3400-kthreads.c:251-259) with only a debug print; msp3400c_detect_stereo is not called anywhere in msp3400c_set_audmode (240-370). The reviewer was probably reading the neighbouring function in the slice. Slice cut the head only.

name: mt9t112_init_pll
prose: Precondition: client is a valid i2c client for the MT9T112 and priv->info->divider holds the PLL divider configuration. Postcondition: every register access made through the mt9t112_reg_write, mt9t112_reg_mask_set and mt9t112_reg_read macros is checked by ECHECKER, which returns the negative status at once if one fails, so on such a failure the function stops there with that negative errno and the later steps are skipped. The sequence is: PLL control register 0x0014 mask set and write of 0x2145; a call to mt9t112_set_pll_dividers with the priv->info->divider values, whose return value is ignored; writes of 0x2525, 0x2527, 0x3427, 0x3027 and later 0x3046 to register 0x0014 with a 10 ms delay between the first group and the next; JPEG-initialisation writes to registers 0x0016, 0x0022, 0x3B84 and 0x002E; mask-set operations on registers 0x0018 and 0x3B82, including the MCU-disable bit (0x0004) and the clearing of the standby bit (0x0001) of register 0x0018, followed by a 50 ms delay; six writes of 0x0001 to register 0x0614 with 1 ms delays between them, which the source labels a standby workaround that disables the secondary I2C pads (they do not take the device out of standby); and a polling loop that reads register 0x0018 up to 100 times, stopping early when bit 0x4000 reads clear and otherwise waiting 10 ms between reads. A failed polling read returns its negative status; if the bit never clears the loop ends after 100 reads without reporting a timeout. It then returns ret, the status of the last checked write (0 on success), so a 0 return does not mean the standby poll succeeded.
note: Reviewer 1 right (timeout not reported); reviewer 2 right that the polling reads' statuses and mt9t112_set_pll_dividers' status are not what is returned, but wrong in implying earlier failures are lost: ECHECKER returns immediately on a negative status (mt9t112.c:53-58), so the old claim 'overwriting failures of earlier writes with later writes' was false; reviewer 3 right: the six 0x0614 writes are the standby workaround that disables secondary I2C pads (453-468), the out-of-standby step is the 0x0018 mask set (449). mt9t112.c:397-480.

name: __mt9v032_set_power
prose: Precondition: mt9v032 points to an initialized mt9v032 device with a usable regmap, clock, optional reset GPIO, model data and control handler. Postcondition: if on is false it calls clk_disable_unprepare on the sensor clock and returns 0. If on is true it calls mt9v032_power_on: that sets the reset GPIO (if any) to 1, calls clk_set_rate(sysclk) and clk_prepare_enable (a failure of either returns its error with the clock not enabled and the reset GPIO still asserted), waits 1 us, releases the reset GPIO if present, and writes MT9V032_RESET = 1, MT9V032_RESET = 0 and MT9V032_CHIP_CONTROL = master mode; a failing register write there calls clk_disable_unprepare and returns the error, with the reset GPIO already released. If power_on succeeded, it writes the pixel clock polarity register (model pclk_reg) only when mt9v032->pdata.clk_pol is non-zero, writes MT9V032_ROW_NOISE_CORR_CONTROL = 0, and returns the result of v4l2_ctrl_handler_setup on the control handler (0 on success). On a failure of the polarity write, the noise-correction write or the control setup it returns that negative error and the clock stays prepared and enabled and the reset GPIO stays released, because this function does not undo the power-on. The function takes no locks itself.
note: Reviewer 1 right (polarity write only if pdata.clk_pol, line 341); reviewer 2 and 3 right: clk_set_rate and clk_prepare_enable failures leave the clock not enabled (mt9v032_power_on 278-285), the reset GPIO is released after power-on succeeded (289-291), and the old prose had both backwards. mt9v032.c:326-354, power_on 271-319.

name: ov02e10_set_ctrl
prose: Precondition: ctrl belongs to ov02e10's ctrl_handler, ov02e10->cur_mode is valid, and for V4L2_CID_VBLANK ov02e10->exposure is a valid control; for HFLIP, VFLIP the hflip and vflip controls exist. Postcondition: if ctrl->id is V4L2_CID_VBLANK it first calls __v4l2_ctrl_modify_range on ov02e10->exposure with the existing minimum and step and with both maximum and default set to cur_mode->height + ctrl->val - OV02E10_EXPOSURE_MAX_MARGIN (this can lower or raise the maximum; the current exposure value is only clamped into the new range, not set to the maximum), and if that returns non-zero it returns that error without writing any register and without a runtime PM reference. It then calls pm_runtime_get_if_in_use; if that returns 0 it returns 0 for every ctrl->id (including unrecognised ones) without writing registers; a negative return from pm_runtime_get_if_in_use is not tested. Otherwise it writes OV02E10_REG_COMMAND_UPDATE = OV02E10_COMMAND_HOLD, its result being stored in ret. For a recognised id it then writes the page register OV02E10_PAGE_1 and the target register: analogue gain, digital gain, exposure, orientation as hflip->val | vflip->val << 1 (for HFLIP or VFLIP), VTS = cur_mode->height + ctrl->val (VBLANK), or the test pattern through ov02e10_test_pattern; for any other id it sets ret to -EINVAL, replacing any earlier error. The register writes use cci_write with ret as the error pointer, so once ret is non-zero the later writes are skipped, including the final write of OV02E10_COMMAND_UPDATE = OV02E10_COMMAND_UPDATE, so after an error (including -EINVAL for an unrecognised id) the register is left at the HOLD value. It then calls pm_runtime_put and returns ret: 0, the first write error, or -EINVAL. No memory is allocated and no locks are taken.
note: Reviewer 1 right (range can narrow); reviewer 2 right (modify_range only clamps the current value); reviewer 3 right (final COMMAND_UPDATE write is skipped when ret is non-zero because cci_write returns *err without writing, e.g. after the default case sets -EINVAL, ov02e10.c:359-365). ov02e10.c:289-370.

name: ov5640_s_stream
prose: Precondition: sd belongs to an ov5640 sensor (to_ov5640_dev(sd)); enable is 0 or non-zero (the comparison sensor->streaming == !enable assumes 0 or 1); the caller does not hold sensor->lock. Postcondition: if enable is non-zero it first calls pm_runtime_resume_and_get (a negative result is returned with no reference held) and v4l2_ctrl_handler_setup (a non-zero result drops the reference with pm_runtime_put and is returned). It then takes sensor->lock; if sensor->streaming equals !enable, then only when enable is non-zero and sensor->pending_mode_change is set it calls ov5640_set_mode, and only when enable is non-zero and sensor->pending_fmt_change is set it calls ov5640_set_framefmt with sensor->fmt and clears pending_fmt_change after that call succeeds (a failure of either goes straight to the exit with that error and the stream is not started or stopped). It then starts or stops the stream with ov5640_set_stream_mipi if ov5640_is_csi2(sensor) holds, or ov5640_set_stream_dvp otherwise, and sets sensor->streaming to enable only if that call returned 0; if sensor->streaming already equals enable, none of this is done and ret is 0. It then releases sensor->lock and, if enable is 0 or ret is non-zero, calls pm_runtime_put_autosuspend on the I2C device whether or not enable was 0 with the stream previously running; otherwise, for enable non-zero and ret 0, the runtime PM reference taken at entry is kept, including the case where the sensor was already streaming and nothing was changed. It returns 0 or the negative error from the failing step.
note: Reviewer 2 right (pending_fmt_change is cleared right after set_framefmt succeeds, line 3739, even if the later set_stream call fails); reviewer 3 right (pending mode/format changes are applied only when enable is non-zero, 3729 and 3735). Extra: the put at 3754-3755 does not depend on streaming having been on, and the entry reference is retained also when streaming==enable. ov5640.c:3709-3759.

name: ov965x_s_stream
prose: Precondition: sd belongs to an initialized ov965x device and the caller does not hold ov965x->lock. Postcondition: it takes ov965x->lock and holds it on every return path except around the v4l2_ctrl_handler_setup call, where it is released and retaken; it is released before returning. If ov965x->streaming equals !on: when on is non-zero it calls __ov965x_set_params; then, whether on is zero or not, if ret is still 0 and ctrls->update is set it releases the lock, calls v4l2_ctrl_handler_setup, retakes the lock and clears ctrls->update only if the setup succeeded; then, if ret is still 0, it writes REG_COM2 with 0x01 (on non-zero) or 0x11 (on zero). If streaming does not equal !on none of that is done and ret stays 0. After that block, regardless of whether it ran, if ret is 0 it adds 1 to ov965x->streaming when on is non-zero or subtracts 1 when on is zero, so the counter changes even when the requested state was already the current one. It then issues WARN_ON if ov965x->streaming is negative (checked whether or not ret is non-zero), releases the lock and returns ret, which is 0 or the first failing result among __ov965x_set_params, v4l2_ctrl_handler_setup and the REG_COM2 write; in that error case streaming is not changed and ctrls->update stays set if the control setup failed.
note: Reviewers 2 and 3 right (streaming is incremented/decremented outside the transition block, lines 1366-1367, so it changes even when streaming != !on; v4l2_ctrl_handler_setup also runs for on=0 when ctrls->update is set, 1350-1361). Reviewer 1 (returns 0 without changing streaming when already in state) wrong for this code: it returns 0 but streaming still moves. ov9650.c:1337-1373.

name: ov965x_s_power
prose: Precondition: sd belongs to an initialized ov965x device, the caller does not hold ov965x->lock, and on is 0 or non-zero (ov965x->power is compared with !on). Postcondition: after a debug message it takes ov965x->lock and releases it before returning. If ov965x->power equals !on it calls __ov965x_set_power(ov965x, on): for on non-zero that calls clk_prepare_enable on the clock (a failure returns its error before any change), releases the power-down and reset GPIOs and sleeps 25 ms; for on zero it asserts the reset and power-down GPIOs and calls clk_disable_unprepare and cannot fail; on its success path it also sets ov965x->streaming to 0. If that succeeded and on is non-zero, it then writes the ov965x_init_regs array with ov965x_write_array and, whatever that write returns, sets ov965x->apply_frame_fmt and ov965x->ctrls.update to 1. If ov965x->power did not equal !on, none of this is done and ret is 0. If ret is 0 at the end (including the case where nothing was done because the power state already matched), it adds 1 to ov965x->power when on is non-zero or subtracts 1 when it is zero, so the counter also changes when the requested state was already current. A WARN_ON fires if ov965x->power is negative (checked whether or not ret is non-zero). It returns 0, the clk_prepare_enable error, or the ov965x_write_array error; if the clock enable fails ov965x->power, streaming and the flags are unchanged, and if the init write fails the hardware remains powered on with streaming cleared and the two flags set, while ov965x->power is not incremented.
note: Reviewer 1 right (power count also changes when already in the requested state), reviewer 2 right (write_array failure leaves hardware powered and flags set; old prose said so for that case but wrongly claimed no flags when set_power failed only), reviewer 3 right (lock is taken after v4l2_dbg, line 536). ov9650.c:529-552, __ov965x_set_power 506-527.
